title: SSO-enriched audit compression & policy controller for cost-aware retention
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: With RBAC v2 and wider SSO/SAML adoption we are ingesting significantly more audit events (identity link events, SAML assertions, admin actions). Storing all raw events at full indexing fidelity is driving storage spend and query cost. We need a pipeline + policy controller that: 1) enriches incoming audit events with SSO/RBAC context, sensitivity scores, and tenant SLAs; 2) applies dynamic compression, indexing level, partitioning, and TTL decisions at ingest time; 3) enforces cost controls and makes retention decisions auditable and reversible for compliance teams. Goal: reduce long-term storage costs by ~40% for non-privileged events while preserving full-fidelity retention for high-sensitivity admin/SAML events and meeting compliance SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest enricher tags >= 99% of audit events with tenant_id, idp_name, rbac_role_hash, sensitivity_score
Policy controller returns a decision for compression_level (none|fast|aggressive), index_level (full|metadata|none), ttl_days and partition_target for >99% of events within 10ms per event at median

End-to-end pipeline with canary enabled stores events according to decisions and query patterns for 'admin:full' events return within SLA (p50 < 200ms) and metadata-only queries return within SLA (p50 < 150ms)
Storage cost projection shows >= 30% reduction for tiered tenants in pilot compared to baseline (same traffic), validated over synthetic replay
Auditability: every retention/compression decision is logged and queryable for a tenant/time range; support export for compliance review
Security review completed for KMS usage and data-at-rest encryption for compressed artifacts
Migration plan and backfill script for converting 30 days of recent data to new indexing policy exist and tested on staging
implementation_notes: Ingest stage: add enricher lambda to audit-stream with SAML/SSO correlation (idp_name, assertion_id) and RBAC v2 resolver that maps actor -> role_hash and role_sensitivity

Decision engine: lightweight policy service that evaluates tenant policy + event sensitivity + retention SLA -> outputs compression_level,index_level,ttl_days,partition_hint. Store policies in Config Service (feature flags for canary).

Compression: use columnar chunking + snappy for fast compress; aggressive mode writes Parquet blobs to coldstore and only stores metadata index; fast mode writes compressed JSON with minimal indices; none keeps existing ingest format.
Indexing: three levels: full (token-level inverted index), metadata-only (actor, action, timestamp, idp, role_hash), none (no secondary index; only primary time/partition lookup).
Partitioning: tenant-hash + day for hot partitioning; provide hot/cold tier routing to allow same tenant data across Tiers. Partition size target ~ 8-32 GB compressed per shard.

TTL & retention: per-policy TTLs enforced by orchestrator that compacts/flushes to coldstore then marks primary index expiration. Retention metadata stored in audit-retention-metadata table for returns by compliance APIs.

Backfill & migration: streaming rewriter reads timeframe, reapplies policy decisions, writes to new partitions, marks old blobs for tombstone and eventual GC. Include idempotency keys and progress checkpoints.
Observability: add new console panels: per-tenant storage-savings, decision-distribution heatmap, per-policy compliance exceptions, and alert on "unexpected_full_indexing" events.
Access controls: only admin roles (via RBAC v2) can change retention policies; policy changes are themselves audited and require two-person approval for high-impact reductions.
Rollout: canary to 5 low-volume tenants, then 25 tenants (mix of dev/prod), then org-wide after validation. Provide rollback toggle in Console to revert to legacy ingestion.
Encryption/KMS: compressed coldstore artifacts must be encrypted with tenant-key or org-key as required by tenant policy; integrate with existing KMS/HSM framework.
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Spike completed comparing compression formats (snappy+parquet vs gzipped JSON). Parquet chunking wins for aggressive coldstore scenario (20-35% better compression, faster query for column scans).

2025-02-16: Enricher prototype implemented and tested on sampled stream. SSO correlation works for AzureAD and Okta; edge case when idp_name missing is tagged 'unknown-idp' and routed to metadata-only by default.

2025-02-17: Policy service prototype with simple rule language (if role_sensitivity >= 8 -> full index + ttl 365; else if tenant_sla == 'low' -> aggressive compression + ttl 30). Performance microbenchmark shows 95th percentile decision latency 12ms; need to optimize to <10ms.

2025-02-18: Security review kickoff flagged requirement: ensure policy changes are RBAC-protected and KMS access for per-tenant keys must use ephemeral credentials. Added dependency on security infra ticket ENG-97210.

2025-02-19: Integration test in staging: canary pipeline stored events correctly and console showed initial storage-savings metrics. Found edge case where replayed events lacked assertion_id -> backfill handles mapping by event-signature.

2025-02-20: Plan to optimize decision service by adding concurrent LRU policy cache to reduce median latency to ~3ms for hot tenants. Scheduling rollout for 2025-02-28 after policy cache and KMS gating are in place.
